features.name: argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms
features.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own argument explicitly compares its claim, case or proposal to an established scientific or historical norm; else 0.
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, makes an explicit comparison between their claim, case or proposal and an established scientific norm (e.g. accepted scientific standard, consensus, or established finding/practice) or an established historical norm (e.g. a long-standing historical standard, practice or precedent), stating similarity or difference to it. Return 0 if the argument contains no such explicit comparison (mere mention of science or history without comparing to a norm does not count). Exclude quotations or positions attributed to others unless the OP adopts them. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they would otherwise qualify; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is not itself a scientific/historical norm comparison. Output a single 0/1 value. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

Return 1 if at least one comment directly quotes wording from the OP's argument text (verbatim or near-verbatim quoted/block-quoted passage that matches the argument), regardless of whether the commenter agrees, disagrees or refutes. Paraphrase without quoted wording, quotes of other comments or external sources, and quoting only the title do not count. Return 0 if the comment list is valid and no comment quotes the argument. If OC_comments is a valid empty list return 0. If OC_comments or argument is missing or malformed return null. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if within the argument or a comment; quoted text consisting of such content does not count. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Use supplied current text, including marked edits; list order carries no meaning. Output a single 0/1 or null.

Return 0 if the comment list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list (0). Ignore as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including within the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Measure current supplied text; do not infer initial snapshots or comment order. Output a single 0/1.

Score the OP's own assertions about their view on a 0-10 integer scale of epistemic certainty conveyed by modality markers. Assumption: aggregate over the whole argument by the overall balance of hedged versus high-certainty markers on the claims central to the OP's position; this aggregation is an operational choice, not a hypothesis requirement. Exclude quotations of other people or reported opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them, and exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain hedged or certain wording; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If the argument is missing, malformed, or contains no assessable OP assertions after exclusions, return null.

members.definition: OC_comments (other users' comments, not the OP): number of comments that contain at least one specific real-world example (an actual case, event, person, institution, or concrete personal experience; not invented or hypothetical).
members.spec: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP. Return the integer count of comments in the list that contain at least one specific real-world example offered in the comment's own argument. A specific real-world example is an actual, concrete case such as a named or identifiable event, person, organization, policy, study, place, or a concrete personal experience of the commenter. Purely invented or hypothetical scenarios, generic generalizations and vague references do not qualify. No outside verification is needed. Count each comment at most once regardless of how many examples it has. Count comments, not distinct commenters. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; these never count as evidence. Generic discussion of delta or platform rules is not an outcome announcement but is not an example unless it is itself a specific real-world case. Range 0 to list length; 0 means no comment has such an example. An empty valid list gives 0. Missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

right_feature.definition: OP argument text: overall epistemic certainty of the OP's own assertions, 0-10 (0 = predominantly modest/uncertain/hedged markers, 10 = predominantly high-modality categorical assertions)
right_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument field (current supplied text, including marked edits). Score the OP's own assertions about their view on a 0-10 integer scale of epistemic certainty conveyed by modality markers. Anchors: 0 = nearly all claims are explicitly modest or uncertain (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'might', 'I could be wrong', 'not sure'); 5 = a roughly even mix of hedged and unhedged claims; 10 = nearly all claims are stated with high-modality/categorical certainty (e.g. 'obviously', 'definitely', 'must', 'always', 'never', 'undeniably') and no hedging. Assumption: aggregate over the whole argument by the overall balance of hedged versus high-certainty markers on the claims central to the OP's position; this aggregation is an operational choice, not a hypothesis requirement. Exclude quotations of other people or reported opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them, and exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain hedged or certain wording; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If the argument is missing, malformed, or contains no assessable OP assertions after exclusions, return null.

Ignore and exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules may be considered. right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP. Return the integer count of comments in the list that contain at least one specific real-world example offered in the comment's own argument. A specific real-world example is an actual, concrete case such as a named or identifiable event, person, organization, policy, study, place, or a concrete personal experience of the commenter. Purely invented or hypothetical scenarios, generic generalizations and vague references do not qualify. No outside verification is needed. Count each comment at most once regardless of how many examples it has. Count comments, not distinct commenters. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; these never count as evidence. Generic discussion of delta or platform rules is not an outcome announcement but is not an example unless it is itself a specific real-world case. Range 0 to list length; 0 means no comment has such an example. An empty valid list gives 0. Missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

left_feature.name: distinct_counterargument_count

left_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), with title and argument only as context to identify the OP's view. Count the distinct counter-arguments the comments make against the OP's view; a counter-argument is a separate reason, objection, or piece of evidence challenging the OP's position. Deduplicate semantically: the same argument repeated in several comments, or restated within one comment, counts once; one comment can contribute several distinct arguments. Do not count agreement with the OP, clarifying questions, jokes, or moderator/bot notices. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even in argument or comments); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is not itself a counter-argument unless it challenges the OP's view. Output a non-negative integer. A valid empty comment list gives 0. If OC_comments is missing or malformed, output null. Use current supplied text; no chronology is implied by list order.

Generic discussion of platform/delta rules by the OP retains eligibility if it is self-referential. left_feature.spec: Read only the title column (the OP's heading). Return 0 if the title has no such markers, including when it is hedged or tentative (e.g. 'generally', 'I think'). Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Ignore any text reporting a view change, delta award, thank-you or resolution update, or the outcome (none expected in titles); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement. If the title is missing or empty, return null. Output a single value: 1, 0, or null.

Row aggregation assumption: judge the comments jointly and give one score reflecting the overall complexity of the counterarguments, rather than a mean or max; this assumption is operational. Do not score quoted text from others as the commenter's own reasoning unless adopted. Ignore and exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules may be considered. right_feature.name: op_argument_epistemic_certainty
right_feature.definition: OP argument text: overall epistemic certainty of the OP's own assertions, 0-10 (0 = predominantly modest/uncertain/hedged markers, 10 = predominantly high-modality categorical assertions)
right_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument field (current supplied text, including marked edits). Score the OP's own assertions about their view on a 0-10 integer scale of epistemic certainty conveyed by modality markers. Anchors: 0 = nearly all claims are explicitly modest or uncertain (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'might', 'I could be wrong', 'not sure'); 5 = a roughly even mix of hedged and unhedged claims; 10 = nearly all claims are stated with high-modality/categorical certainty (e.g. 'obviously', 'definitely', 'must', 'always', 'never', 'undeniably') and no hedging. Assumption: aggregate over the whole argument by the overall balance of hedged versus high-certainty markers on the claims central to the OP's position; this aggregation is an operational choice, not a hypothesis requirement. Exclude quotations of other people or reported opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them, and exclude moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain hedged or certain wording; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If the argument is missing, malformed, or contains no assessable OP assertions after exclusions, return null.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it), plus the OP's title and argument as the reference text for matching. Count a comment as quoting if it directly reproduces (verbatim or near-verbatim, typically in quotation marks or block quote) wording that appears in the OP's title or argument; the quote need not be endorsed or refuted. Do not count quotations of other sources, paraphrases without reproduced wording, or topic mentions. Ignore as OP reference text any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; a quote matching only such text does not count. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules remains eligible. Use current supplied text including marked edits; do not attempt to reconstruct an initial snapshot. Output the number of quoting comments divided by total number of comments, a value in [0,1] (0 if no comment quotes OP text). Valid empty comment list or malformed/missing OC_comments: null. If a comment's quote cannot be matched because the OP title and argument are both missing, return null unless a match was positively established. List order carries no meaning.

Return 1 if the OP in their own voice recounts at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific experience, event or situation the OP personally lived or directly witnessed (e.g., 'when I worked at...', 'my friend told me / happened to me'). right_feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP context to identify OP's components) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, parse first). Return 1 if at least one single comment (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific component (a particular claim, premise or point) of the OP's argument is valid/correct/reasonable, and then (b) presents a counter-example (a specific case or instance that counters the OP's view or claim), with the acknowledgment coming before the counter-example in that same comment. Acknowledgment and counter-example must be in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Generic politeness, vague agreement, or acknowledgment of the OP as a whole without a specific component does not count; a counter-argument without a counter-example does not count. Judge only comment text; quotation marks alone do not establish validity acknowledgment. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list (0). Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if OP context is missing such that the targeted component cannot be determined. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they appear in the argument or comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement. Use current supplied text, including marked edits, with no initial-snapshot inference. Output a single 0/1 or null.

Return null if argument is missing or malformed; an assessable argument with no marker gives 0. Output a single 0/1 value.

right_feature.spec: Read the OP title and argument (for identifying the OP's specific examples/anecdotes) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly refutes (argues against, contradicts or debunks) a specific example or anecdote that the OP provided, judged within that single comment. Return 0 if no comment does so (e.g., comments only address the general premise, or only agree/mention an example without refuting it). Empty valid comment list -> 0. Missing/malformed OC_comments, or missing OP text needed to identify OP examples -> null. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even inside the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement. Comment order is not meaningful. Use current supplied text; do not infer initial snapshots.

left_feature.name: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_divergence

Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Use current supplied text; no initial snapshot is inferred, and list order is not chronology.

Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they contain hedged or certain wording; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order carries no rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment itself cites a specific, localized example as part of its counter-argument: a particular concrete case, instance, named or identifiable person, place, event, or specific personal experience (real or documented), as opposed to only general principles, abstract claims, broad statistics or generic hypotheticals. The example need not be externally verified; it need not be among any illustrative examples. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so. Return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement but is not itself a specific example. Output a single 0/1 or null.

left_feature.name: op_argument_explicit_uncertainty
left_feature.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit uncertainty marker (e.g., hedge or stated doubt about their own claims); else 0.
left_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, uses at least one explicit marker of uncertainty about their own claims or view (e.g., 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'maybe', 'possibly', 'to my knowledge', 'I think' used as a hedge, stated doubt). Return 0 if the argument is assessable and has no such marker. Do not count uncertainty in quoted external text or attributed to others, rhetorical questions that are not expressions of the OP's own doubt, or moderator/bot notices. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the view changed (even inside argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Do not attempt to reconstruct an initial version; do not remove edits except for outcome-reporting text. If argument is missing or malformed, return null.

right_feature.spec: Read title, argument (for the OP's claim as target) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own text, recounts a concrete personal anecdote from the commenter's own specific experience (or that of someone they personally know) that illustrates real-world consequences of the OP's claim (consequences arising if the claim holds or is acted on). Return 0 if no comment does (comments are only abstract/theoretical arguments, general facts, hypotheticals/invented scenarios, or others' quoted experiences not adopted by the commenter). Quoted OP text or quoted opponents' positions do not count as the commenter's own anecdote. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither such an announcement nor an anecdote by itself. Use current supplied text; do not infer timing or order. Empty comment list -> 0. Missing/malformed OC_comments, or missing title and argument so the claim cannot be identified -> null. Output a single 0/1.

left_feature.name: op_argument_acknowledges_counterargument_or_limitation
left_feature.definition: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument to, or a limitation of, their own view; else 0.
left_feature.spec: Read only the argument column (the OP's own text, current supplied version including any marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument to their view or a limitation/weakness/exception of their own position (e.g. 'a counterpoint is...', 'I admit this may not hold when...', 'one weakness of my view is...'). Illustrative phrasings are not exhaustive. Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment is present. Do not count merely hedging language without naming a counter-argument or limitation, quoted text from other users or opposing positions the OP does not adopt, or moderator/bot notices. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the view changed (including in edits); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Do not attempt to reconstruct an initial snapshot by removing edits. If argument is missing or malformed, return null. Output a single value: 1, 0, or null.

right_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. If missing/malformed return null; if a valid list is empty return null. Anchors: 0 = no reasoning; 2 = single simple assertion, one-sided with no qualification; 4 = some reasons but little differentiation; 6 = several distinct considerations or acknowledgment of alternative views/conditions; 8 = clear differentiation plus integration of perspectives, with qualifications; 10 = highly differentiated, integrated, nuanced multi-perspective reasoning. Row aggregation assumption: judge the comments jointly and give one score reflecting the overall complexity of the counterarguments, rather than a mean or max; this assumption is operational. Do not score quoted text from others as the commenter's own reasoning unless adopted. Ignore and exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules may be considered. Output one number 0-10 or null.

right_feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself uses second-person direct address (addressing the OP/reader directly with 'you', 'your', imperative addressed to them, etc.) in the commenter's own words. Quoted text from the OP or others does not count unless the commenter adopts it as their own address. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does. Valid empty list -> 0. Missing or malformed list -> null. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting the outcome; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed but is not itself second-person evidence unless it addresses the OP directly. left_feature.name: any_comment_presents_counterargument
left_feature.definition: Other-user OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment presents a counterargument to the OP's stated view (title/argument); else 0.
left_feature.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Title and argument give the OP's view, needed to identify the target. Return 1 if at least one comment in OC_comments presents a counterargument, i.e. a reason, evidence or reasoning offered against the OP's stated view or its supporting claims; agreement-only, pure questions without argumentative challenge, jokes, moderator/bot notices and off-topic remarks do not count. Partial counterarguments count; the comment need not be correct or persuasive. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies. If OC_comments is empty (valid empty list) return 0. If OC_comments is missing/malformed, or the OP title/argument needed to identify the target is missing, return null. Ignore and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even inside argument or comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Do not use conversation or any outcome column. Output a single 0/1 or null.

right_feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP's text) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes wording from the OP's title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim, e.g. in quotation marks or markdown blockquote, matching available OP text); the comment need not agree with or refute the quote. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty and no comment contains such a quote (paraphrase, summary or topic mention alone does not count; quoting other users, external sources, or non-OP text does not count). Return 0 for a valid empty comment list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if title/argument is missing so that a negative cannot be established (a clear positive match to the available OP text still yields 1). Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including within argument or quoted in comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement and may be used. Use current supplied text; do not infer initial snapshots or chronology; comment order carries no meaning. Output one 0/1 value or null per row.

left_feature.name: counterargument_cognitive_complexity
left_feature.definition: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): overall cognitive complexity of the counterarguments, 0-10 anchored score
left_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. If missing/malformed return null; if a valid list is empty return null. Rate the cognitive complexity of the counterarguments' own reasoning on an integer 0-10 scale: differentiation (recognizing multiple perspectives, distinctions, conditions, trade-offs) and integration (relating those perspectives into a reasoned synthesis or qualified conclusion). Anchors: 0 = no reasoning; 2 = single simple assertion, one-sided with no qualification; 4 = some reasons but little differentiation; 6 = several distinct considerations or acknowledgment of alternative views/conditions; 8 = clear differentiation plus integration of perspectives, with qualifications; 10 = highly differentiated, integrated, nuanced multi-perspective reasoning. Row aggregation assumption: judge the comments jointly and give one score reflecting the overall complexity of the counterarguments, rather than a mean or max; this assumption is operational. Do not score quoted text from others as the commenter's own reasoning unless adopted. Ignore and exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules may be considered. Output one number 0-10 or null.

right_feature.spec: Read only the OP's argument text (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges that alternative perspectives, viewpoints or interpretations to their own view exist (e.g., noting that others may see it differently, or that other reasonable positions exist). Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment is present. Do not count quoted or reported opponents' positions unless the OP explicitly adopts them as acknowledged alternatives, and do not count mere topic mentions. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Return null if the argument is missing or malformed.

left_feature.name: counterargument_cognitive_complexity
left_feature.definition: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): overall cognitive complexity of the counterarguments, 0-10 anchored score
left_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. If missing/malformed return null; if a valid list is empty return null. Rate the cognitive complexity of the counterarguments' own reasoning on an integer 0-10 scale: differentiation (recognizing multiple perspectives, distinctions, conditions, trade-offs) and integration (relating those perspectives into a reasoned synthesis or qualified conclusion). Anchors: 0 = no reasoning; 2 = single simple assertion, one-sided with no qualification; 4 = some reasons but little differentiation; 6 = several distinct considerations or acknowledgment of alternative views/conditions; 8 = clear differentiation plus integration of perspectives, with qualifications; 10 = highly differentiated, integrated, nuanced multi-perspective reasoning. Row aggregation assumption: judge the comments jointly and give one score reflecting the overall complexity of the counterarguments, rather than a mean or max; this assumption is operational. Do not score quoted text from others as the commenter's own reasoning unless adopted. Ignore and exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules may be considered. Output one number 0-10 or null.

right_feature.spec: Read only OC_comments, a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. Return 1 if at least one comment itself employs a specific, concrete illustrative example to illustrate or support its counter-argument: a particular named or described case, instance, event, scenario, or personal experience, rather than only abstract principles or generalities. Real or hypothetical concrete examples count if they are specific and concrete; vague generic references (e.g. 'many people', 'some cases') do not. Examples need not be externally verified. Judge each comment's own argument; a quoted passage from someone else counts only if the comment uses it as its own illustrative example. Ignore any text reporting the OP's view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible but is not itself an example. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including when the list is empty. Return null if OC_comments is missing or cannot be parsed. Output a single 0/1 value.
